reasons.A: Modern, plain voice with short, even sentences, few semicolons and a mild conversational register; it lacks the long semicolon-chained periods and Edwardian assertiveness of the passage.
reasons.B: Closest sentence movement: long semicolon-linked periods, 'I find that' / 'It is true that' openings, confiding-yet-assertive stance and period diction ('any one', 'a man who'), with a 'let them have it' close that echoes the author's cadence without overdoing it.
reasons.C: Period feel and semicolons are right, but it leans on hedges ('I think', 'I believe', 'perhaps'), a rhetorical question and ornamental images ('hens on a perch', dark streets) that push past the passage's plainer argument toward pastiche.
